Implementation notes:

1. Header: Ensure the logo is an accessible element, image, with a label, so it can be focused with VoiceOver and is announced, for instance, as "Firefox"
2. Main content: if the graphic is meaningful, ensure it has meaningful accessibility label. At the same time if the image is more decorative, the importantForAccessibility could be set to false so the image is not focusable with VoiceOver (is marked up as decorative)

Implementation notes:

1. Header: If these images are not functional (tapping on them does not do anything), they could be exposed to accessibility / TalkBack as one custom image view, so a user would need only one swipe (focus stop) to hear both, i.e. "FIrefox: Private Mode"
2. Main content: if the graphic is meaningful, ensure it has meaningful contentDescription. At the same time if the image is more decorative, the contentDescription could be omitted so the image is not focusable with TalkBack (is marked up as decorative)

Implementation note: ensure that the status message is being announced to a user of TalkBack. One way may be to use announceForAccessibility, but in this case better option would be to move the focus to the status message text and then ensure the "Undo" button is the next in the traversal order.

Implementation note: ensure all image buttons have accessible name, i.e. "Clear session" button, "3 private tabs" button, "More" button (or "Settings").

For the button with number of tabs, ensure the accessible name (content description) of the button is being updated when the number of tabs is changed

Implementation note: ensure that this status message is posted with notification (i.e. layoutChanged or screenChanged) so a VoiceOver would be made aware about new element being added to the view and it will be announced for a user
Color contrast increase is recommended here as well
Increasing color contrast is also recommended here, as it was for the AD mockup above

Color contrast of this text is not sufficient on the right side of the tooltip: the lighter part of the gradient against the white text gives only up to 4:1 color contrast ratio while 4.5:1 or higher is expected for the text of this size

1. Could we add an underline for the link?

AFAIK it was recently decided to unify hyperlinks to have underline by default. While it may be only set for desktop, I think it is very solid indication of the difference between the link and its surrounding static text, that also does not rely on use of color alone.

2. Also, the color contrast for the link text is low for the regular text like it - the color contrast for the purple text against the indigo background provides only 3.9:1 ratio while 4.5:1 or higher is expected for the text of this size

@Misha Bruk is this doorhanger actionable? if not, it would need to be an alert.

when the trashcan icon button is pressed with keyboard, the focus should move to the dialog, i.e. to the checkbox "Always ask me, checked". When the dialog is marked up correctly (it has role=dialog and aria-label or aria-labelledby, see Full Page Translations or Security doorhangers), a screen reader would still announce that it is in the dialog, would announce the dialog's label and would read the dialog's full content, then proceeding to announce the focused element, so a blind user would still know what is the doorhanger is about.

Pressing Tab would move the focus to the "Cancel" button > tab to "Delete session data".

OR the initial focus could land on the doorhanger dialog container itself (with tabindex=-1), then pressing Tab would move the visual focus to the checkbox etc.

When the dialog is dismissed by Escape or by pressing either of buttons, the focus should land back on the trashcan icon button (unless the entire window is refreshed, then the focus would be managed by the default browser behavior itself)

"Learn more" link is either the 2nd focusable element or the 1st one (if we want to force users to use the awesomebar still).
